key_insight: In ordered microporous viscoelastic flow, elastic stress strands first trigger chaos, then can reorganize into a more ordered state at higher Weissenberg numbers, producing non-monotonic chaos and pressure-drop trends.
engineering_relevance: Designing porous media and operating conditions around the critical Weissenberg number and solid volume fraction could help control drag, flow stability, and process performance in polymer-processing and filtration systems.
method: Numerical study of viscoelastic flow through a staggered array of cylindrical micropillars.
Tracks birefringent high-stress strands, flow chaos, and pressure-drop components versus Weissenberg number.
Examines how changing solid volume fraction shifts instability onset and the non-monotonic regime.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports statistically stationary flow quantities for the mean pressure drop and identifies a fluctuating contribution that varies non-monotonically with Weissenberg number, alongside a critical instability threshold.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on an ordered microporous geometry, so behavior may differ in disordered media or under different constitutive models and flow conditions.
paper_title: Non-monotonic variations in pressure drop and chaos in viscoelastic fluid flows through an ordered microporous medium
